First, we must convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{9{x}^{2}+1}{(3x+1)^{3}}=\frac{A}{3x+1}+\frac{B}{(3x+1)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(3x+1)^{3}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(3x+1)^{3}$ and get

$$
9{x}^{2}+1=A(3x+1)^{2}+B(3x+1)+C.
$$

Plugging in $x=-\frac{1}{3},$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}9{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}+1 & =A{(3\cdot (-\frac{1}{3})+1)}^{2}+B(3\cdot (-\frac{1}{3})+1)+C \\ 2 & =C\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known value of $C,$ we get an equation relating $A$ and $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}9(0)^{2}+1 & =A(3(0)+1)^{2}+B(3(0)+1)+C \\ 1 & =A+B+2 \\ A+B & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, plugging in $x=-1$ and substituting the known value of $C,$ we get an equation relating $A$ and $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}9(-1)^{2}+1 & =A(3(-1)+1)^{2}+B(3(-1)+1)+C \\ 10 & =4A-2B+2 \\ 4A-2B & =8 \\ 2A-B & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations $2A-B=4$ and $A+B=-1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3A & =4-1 \\ A & =1,\end{aligned}
$$

and substituting back into $A+B=-1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}1+B & =-1 \\ B & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum

$$
\frac{9{x}^{2}+1}{(3x+1)^{3}}=\frac{1}{3x+1}-\frac{2}{(3x+1)^{2}}+\frac{2}{(3x+1)^{3}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{9{x}^{2}+1}{(3x+1)^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{3x+1}-\frac{2}{(3x+1)^{2}}+\frac{2}{(3x+1)^{3}})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{3x+1}\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{1}{(3x+1)^{2}}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{(3x+1)^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+1|+\frac{2}{3(3x+1)}-\frac{1}{3(3x+1)^{2}}+K,\end{aligned}
$$

where $K$ is an integral constant.
